title: Hierarchical physical phase inference with range-normalized lateral action coordinates
coverage_gap: Revision feedback leaves an unresolved off-diagonal extrapolation gap: A2 is the q3 winner with score .475, but both cross-sign E cells are 0/5 for every initial candidate. A2's C cells are HL 8/10 and LH 4/10. Low support action loss and reported IID success do not establish systematic recombination. The supplied failure categories say only native_truncated, so they do not localize grasp versus carry versus seating failures.
reusable_regularity: Two linked hypotheses revise A2: phase inference should respect conditional physical dependencies, and horizontal corrective action magnitude should be represented relative to current geometric range. Replace A2's flat phase head by engagement, vertical-progress and alignment heads. Engagement is goal-independent; vertical progress is independent of planar target position; alignment uses target distance and projected motion rather than factor signs. Retain learned world-axis DP actions but express the x coordinate in a smooth positive range-dependent unit, with associated reach/seating x features normalized by local ranges and scales explicitly retained. This is an invertible coordinate transform, not a prescribed control action, task planner or exact symmetry assumption.
dependencies_preserved: Keep A2's hand/handle and ring/peg learned encoders, soft gates with .25 floor, nine direct relative-coordinate channels and sixteen robot/world channels. Peg information never vanishes from conditioning.

The engagement head sees hand-to-handle xyz, aperture/change, hand/handle increments, ring height and vertical lever-arm information, without any goal. The vertical head sees hand/handle/ring/goal heights, vertical hand/handle increments, aperture and hand-to-handle vertical gap; it can distinguish upward lifting from downward seating at similar heights without seeing goal_x or goal_y.

The alignment head sees planar ring-to-peg distance, handle motion projected along the observed seating direction, ring/goal height error, ring height and aperture. Its probability changes only the transport-versus-seating split, not the upstream engagement/lift probabilities.

Coarse absolute world hand xyz, current world wxyz quaternion, native hand/handle increments, goal/ring heights, previous quaternion inputs and aperture/change retain workspace, fixed-gripper orientation, gravity and contact dependence. Only declared absent object2 fields are omitted.

Separate hand-to-handle, ring-to-handle and ring-to-peg relations preserve the physical lever arm. Explicit reach/seat range channels make their normalized x coordinates metrically recoverable; world position is not deleted to impose an invalid robot symmetry.

The action unit is a positive scalar computed solely from the current physical ring/hand/handle/goal positions. It is fixed for the full sixteen-action chunk. Native y, z and gripper channels remain unchanged; only the host performs native action clipping and execution.

evidence_refs.detail: A1 score .375; A2 .47500000000000003; A3 .25. A2 uniquely selected by record_selection. All cross-sign E cells fail; A3's C=.1 did not support inheriting its global yaw chart/joint diffusion bundle.
Locally recorded feedback facts, selection arithmetic, lack of stage diagnoses and the exact structural revision rationale
The same ten exact support episodes only, no added demonstrations or transformed synthetic trajectories
Both manipulated factors are along world x. Native action scale .01 m, fixed rotation, handle-site object_xyz and separate physical ring_center_xyz. Table-level initial nut_z=.02 and goal_z=.1.

Previously inspected obs 0:3, 25:29 and 38:43: ring near .019 m before pickup and above .08 m during lift, with a persistent handle/ring lever arm. Actions 26:31 show the lift transition. These support a broad .025-to-.08 m smooth blend of range units, not a contact oracle.
Previously inspected obs 59:62 and 86:90 show elevated transport and descent at similar horizontal alignment; vertical direction distinguishes lift from lowering despite overlapping heights.
Causal encode/decode and learned module registration contract
Common encoded action4 epsilon objective and separate mask-normalized auxiliary loss remain unchanged

expected_failure_signature: Falsifiable: A4 should raise the equal-cell C/E score over A2 if the linked phase/range hypotheses matter, particularly on LH and cross-sign E. Failure to improve cross-sign E would argue that these biases are insufficient, not justify a later checkpoint or extra slot. The new range unit can amplify the wrong learned x direction, underact near zero error, or poorly match clipped expert actions; a failed grasp can also change the range blend prematurely. Hierarchical phase restrictions can misinterpret contact recovery, and vertical-only progress inference can confuse initial approach with descent unless the engagement gate works. Development feedback does not yet identify any of these as observed failure causes. The bundled revision does not isolate the individual causal benefit of its two changes.

required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42] and raw_current [B,42]. Learned phase estimates use raw_history; action scaling uses raw_current. No labels, masks, episode indices or elapsed-time clock at inference.
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: World-aligned, range-dependent x unit; no rotation or additive reference action. At chunk start let rg=sqrt((handle_x-hand_x)^2+.025^2)/.1 and rs=sqrt((goal_x-ring_x)^2+.025^2)/.1. Let u=clamp((ring_z-.025)/(.08-.025),0,1), w=u^2*(3-2*u), and sx=sqrt((1-w)*rg^2+w*rs^2), so sx>=.25. Encode (ax,ay,az,gripper) as (ax/sx,ay,az,gripper); decode as (sx*ux,uy,uz,ug). All sixteen positions use that same causal sx. Native xyz remains .01 m per decoded unit. Zero encoded action maps to zero native action, action direction remains learned, and the candidate never clips actions. The clamp here is only a geometric feature blend. The host clips the decoded native cube and executes four of sixteen actions.
required_runtime_fields.range_conditioning: Per-history grasp_x and seating_x are divided by rg and rs respectively before metric scaling. Append per-history rg, rs and the shared current chunk sx so the denoiser knows the action unit and the original ranges.

training_only_targets.name: phase
training_only_targets.source: Unchanged from actual parent A2: exact D_N obs[k] and native actions[k] only.
training_only_targets.definition: Priority order: lift=1 if native az>.6 and ring_z<.18; seating=3 if ring_z>.06 and planar goal-to-ring distance<.04; transport=2 if ring_z>.1; otherwise acquisition=0. Coarse motion annotations are not physical contact truth or runtime labels.
training_only_targets.prediction: Let e,r,a be sigmoid outputs of engagement, vertical-progress and alignment heads. Phase probabilities are [1-e, e*(1-r), e*r*(1-a), e*r*a]. Their product structure makes the supervision conditional: acquisition NLL need not teach target alignment; lift NLL need not classify near/far target states.
training_only_targets.loss: Same weight .05 and NLL form as A2. Each of two historical-label losses is weighted by mask[:,0] and the sum is divided by 2*sum(mask[:,0]) with denominator floor 1. The public four-channel action epsilon objective remains weight 1 and denominator 4*mask.sum(). No auxiliary joint diffusion channels, counterfactual rollouts or future motion conditions are introduced.

support_fit_statistics: None. No support-fit regression, optimization, cached trajectories, external data or pretrained weights. Physical constants are explicit design choices; all training targets come from the same exact D_N. Empty deployment state is sufficient.
architecture: One unchanged common DP factory invocation with condition_dim=96, diffusion action_dim=4. Retain A2 grasp MLP 26->64->32 and seating MLP 28->64->32. Replace flat 16->64->4 phase network by 13->64->1 engagement, 8->64->1 vertical and 5->64->1 alignment MLPs, SiLU hidden activations. Concatenate 32+32 branch latents, 4 phase probabilities, 16 world/contact-motion channels, 9 normalized direct relations and 3 range channels. All modules are registered only in build_modules and participate in the joint loss; common U-Net, optimizer, updates, horizons, masks and success semantics are not changed.
change_summary: One new A4 training slot based on q3-selected A2. Retain its two encoders, world/geometry dependencies, phase annotations, .25 gate floor and .05 auxiliary weight. Introduce hierarchical dependency-restricted phase inference and a nonsingular, world-aligned lateral range coordinate in both representation and action encoding/decoding; append explicit scales, changing condition width from 93 to 96. A3 is negative comparative feedback, not an inherited parent. Initial A4 files have no structural repairs or performance-driven repeated debug. A1-A3 remain immutable.
